newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares make cautious advance.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares make cautious advance.

text.p: Austrian shares finished up on Friday but, in a session characterised by low turnover, failed to keep pace with an impressive rally in neighbouring Germany.
Traders forecast prices would continue gently upwards in the coming week ahead of the expiry of June ATX futures on Friday. "We have entered a consolidation phase," a dealer said.
The blue-chip ATX index closed 6.21 points, or 0.48 percent, higher at 1,302.29, taking its cue from strong performances across Europe and on Wall Street.
In the 21-share index 11 gainers outnumbered eight losers. Two shares were unchanged.

High-grade steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm slumped 39 schillings in the closing minutes, knocked down by a 100-lot sell order. Boehler closed at 930 schillings, nine up on the day but well below the 969 session high.
"It is incomprehensible what happened there," a trader said.
Engineering group VA Technologie was the biggest ATX gainer, up 30.8 schillings, or 1.43 percent, at 2,186. Papermaker Leykam and oil group OMV also posted gains.
Viscose fibre maker Lenzing was the leading decliner. Its shares finished 6.5 schillings, or 0.88 percent, down at 731 schillings.
June ATX futures stood 6.1 points up at 1,305. The broad-based Vienna bourse index was 1.56 points up at 477.87. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 254
